newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe authorities warned over export zone sites.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe authorities warned over export zone sites.

text.p: A senior government official on Monday urged Zimbabwean authorities to locate the southern African country's unfolding export processing zones (EPZs) in economically-viable and not politically-expedient areas.

"As we proceed with this programme, those who make the decisions must guard against the temptation of locating the EPZs in certain areas simply for political reasons because that would be economically disastrous," said Vincent Kwenda, an under- secretary in Zimbabwe's ministry of industry and commerce.

He was speaking at the start of a two-day national seminar on the development of export processing zones, and was refering to a clamour by several local authorities, including some remote rural centres, to host the EPZs.
Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe's government adopted a programme on EPZs early this year, five years later than initially planned, citing it needed more time to prepare the ground.
So far the Zimbabwe EPZ Authority had approved four projects, one of which was already operational, and five others which were under consideration, Kwenda said.

Only companies exporting 80 percent of their products are eligible to apply for an EPZ licence, and they can either operate from their own sites or relocate to still to be designated zones, enjoying benefits such as a five-year tax holiday and later a 15 percent corporate tax instead of the current 37.5 percent.

"Where we get zones...the idea is to have them in economically viable districts, where transport, communication and skilled labour is easily available," Kwenda said, adding the EPZs were aimed at improving international competitiveness.
